Former President Donald Trump is a defendant in a sizable number of criminal and civil cases. To help readers parse through these complex legal developments, we have centralized information on Trump’s major cases in the most comprehensive clearinghouse of its kind. Below you will find links to relevant court proceedings, key statutes, government documents, and defense documents – as well as *Just Security* resources and analysis, media and other guides.

Latest Update: As of July 10, 2026, two of this guide’s central storylines have moved. On June 30, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Trump v. Barbara that Trump’s executive order ending birthright citizenship violates the 14th Amendment, upholding automatic citizenship for children born on U.S. soil. Trump announced on July 8, 2026 that he will ask the Court for a rehearing, an outcome legal experts call a long shot since the Court hasn’t granted one in a merits case since 1965. Separately, Trump’s $10 billion IRS lawsuit, which he settled and voluntarily dismissed in May 2026 in exchange for a $1.776 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund,” was reopened by a federal judge on July 1, 2026 after 35 former federal judges challenged the settlement as collusive.

S3.retrieval_query: What primary records (court orders, settlements, or regulatory actions) document any ban on Eric Trump, Donald J. Trump Jr., or Ivanka Trump operating a charity, and what is its stated scope and duration?

passages.P1: Latest Update: As of July 10, 2026, two of this guide’s central storylines have moved. On June 30, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Trump v. Barbara that Trump’s executive order ending birthright citizenship violates the 14th Amendment, upholding automatic citizenship for children born on U.S. soil. Trump announced on July 8, 2026 that he will ask the Court for a rehearing, an outcome legal experts call a long shot since the Court hasn’t granted one in a merits case since 1965. Separately, Trump’s $10 billion IRS lawsuit, which he settled and voluntarily dismissed in May 2026 in exchange for a $1.776 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund,” was reopened by a federal judge on July 1, 2026 after 35 former federal judges challenged the settlement as collusive.
passages.P3: The Trump lawsuit story in 2026 is unlike anything in American legal history. Over 530 lawsuits were filed against the Trump administration in its first year alone. That number has kept climbing.
passages.P4: From states suing over immigration orders to Trump personally suing his own government for $10 billion, the legal battles touch almost every corner of American life. Tariffs, DOGE cuts, birthright citizenship, federal funding, and worker rights are all in play.
passages.P5: Related: Trump Voting Rights Lawsuits 2026: All Key Cases Explained
passages.P6: This guide breaks down every major category. Plain English. No fluff. Just the facts you need to understand what’s happening and what it means for you.
passages.P8: A Trump lawsuit refers to any legal action filed either against Donald Trump, against his administration’s policies, or by Trump himself against other parties. In 2025 and 2026, these cases span two very different directions.
passages.P9: The first direction: hundreds of lawsuits filed by states, civil rights groups, labor unions, and individuals challenging the Trump administration’s executive orders and policy actions.
passages.P10: The second direction: lawsuits filed by Trump personally, most notably a $10 billion suit against his own federal government over leaked tax returns.
passages.P11:
| Type | Who Filed | What It Challenges |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Against Trump Admin | States, nonprofits, unions | Executive orders, funding cuts, deportations |
| By Trump | Trump personally | IRS leak, DOJ investigations |
| Business/historical | Private parties | Contracts, defamation, property |
passages.P12: Both directions involve billions of dollars and Supreme Court-level constitutional questions. Both affect ordinary Americans.
passages.P13: ## How Many Lawsuits Against Trump Have Been Filed?
passages.P14: Legal analysts estimate that 20 to 30 of the 530 current lawsuits against the Trump administration are likely to reach the Supreme Court.
passages.P15: As of January 3, 2026, the Associated Press was tracking 358 cases, grouping them into 14 categories including immigration, DOGE cuts, and civil liberties.
passages.P16: President Donald Trump was facing roughly 400 lawsuits from his executive orders, far more than had been filed at the same point during his first term.
passages.P17:
| Time Period | Lawsuits Filed | Key Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First 100 days (2025) | 100+ | Immigration, funding, DOGE |
| By end of 2025 | 530+ | All policy areas |
| As of early 2026 | 600+ | Tariffs, birthright citizenship, climate |
passages.P18: No president in history has faced this volume of legal challenges in such a short period. That’s not a partisan opinion. It’s the documented conclusion of organizations tracking the cases across the political spectrum.
